hints.title: In-Place Character Inversion Obstacle
hints.text: Creating a reversed copy allocates linear extra buffer space. How can you mirror characters around the center index using only constant additional space?

hints.title: Converging Boundary Mirroring
hints.text: Start with boundary markers at both endpoints of the character buffer and swap their values while moving them toward the center until they meet.

hints.title: Two Pointer Swap Procedure
hints.text: Set left to zero and right to the final index. While left is strictly less than right, swap characters at left and right, then increment left and decrement right.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of character array (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: In-place two-pointer character reversal with O(1) extra space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Constructing a new reversed string or list allocates O(N) memory, failing the O(1) in-place requirement.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Opposite-end swaps perform exactly N/2 operations with zero heap allocation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correct loop termination (left < right) and safe in-place swapping.
